definitions.gloss: presence at a scene; being on-site; attending in person
definitions.explanation: The act of being present at a particular location, especially an official or important scene such as a crime scene or event.

examples.japanese: ⟦{刑事|けいじ}→刑事：02741_keiji⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{現場|げんば}→現場：02723_genba⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{臨場|りんじょう}⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The detective arrived at the scene.

examples.japanese: ⟦{検察官|けんさつかん}→検察官：09664_kensatsukan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{事故|じこ}→事故：00851_jiko⟧⟦{現場|げんば}→現場：02723_genba⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{臨場|りんじょう}⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{調査|ちょうさ}→調査：03489_chousa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{行|おこな}った→行う：01238_okonau⟧。
examples.english: The prosecutor was present at the accident scene and conducted an investigation.

examples.japanese: {臨場|りんじょう}⟦{検査|けんさ}→検査：02707_kensa⟧。

notes:
A formal and legal term for being present at a scene, especially of police, prosecutors or inspectors. In everyday language it is met mostly in the compound ⟦{臨場感|りんじょうかん}→臨場感：06251_rinjoukan⟧ (a sense of being there, realism), which has its own entry.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{現場|げんば}→現場：02723_genba⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{臨場|りんじょう}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to be present at the scene
- {臨場|りんじょう}⟦{検査|けんさ}→検査：02707_kensa⟧: on-site inspection
- ⟦{臨場感|りんじょうかん}→臨場感：06251_rinjoukan⟧: sense of being there; immersiveness

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {立|た}ち{会|あ}い: attendance; witnessing — being present as a witness or observer
- ⟦{現場|げんば}→現場：02723_genba⟧: scene; site — the location itself, not the act of being there
- ⟦{出動|しゅつどう}→出動：28803_shutsudou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to be dispatched; to go out (on duty) — focuses on the deployment rather than the presence
